title: What is a backdoor Roth (in 30 seconds)
hook: Income too high for a Roth? Backdoor.

concepts.title: The problem: direct contribution is phased out
concepts.body: Single filers above $168,000 in 2026 can't contribute directly to a Roth IRA. Married filing jointly above $252,000 — same door closed. Earned income, no room left.

concepts.title: The two-step workaround: non-deductible trad + convert
concepts.body: Put after-tax money into a traditional IRA — non-deductible contribution, so no tax deduction. Then convert it to a Roth. The conversion is tax-free because you already paid tax on the money going in.

concepts.title: The gotcha: pro-rata rule
concepts.body: If you have other pre-tax IRA money, the IRS aggregates it. The conversion becomes partly taxable in proportion to your existing pre-tax balance. Zero pre-tax IRAs elsewhere? Backdoor is clean. Otherwise — the pro-rata rule applies.

sources: IRS — Roth IRA income phaseout limits (IR-2025-111, Nov 13 2025)
IRS Pub 590-A — Backdoor Roth IRA strategy
IRS Form 8606 — Nondeductible Traditional IRA contributions and Roth conversions
